name: Refrigerator Door Shelf Bin
description: Genuine OEM clear door bin with white trim. Holds jars, bottles and condiments on the interior fridge door. Tool-free, snap-in installation.
install_steps: Open the refrigerator door fully to reach the old bin.
Push up gently on the bottom of the bin to release it from the door rails.
Tilt the bin outward and lift it free.
Line the new bin up with the rails at the same height.
Press down firmly until it clicks securely into place.

name: Refrigerator Ice Maker Assembly
description: Complete OEM ice maker assembly with motor, mold and ejector. Replaces a unit that has stopped producing or ejecting ice.
install_steps: Unplug the refrigerator or switch off the breaker.
Remove the ice bin and unscrew the ice maker mounting screws.
Disconnect the wiring harness from the old assembly.
Mount the new assembly and reconnect the harness.
Reinstall the screws and ice bin, restore power, and allow 24 hours to produce ice.

name: Refrigerator Water Inlet Valve
description: OEM dual water inlet valve that feeds the ice maker and water dispenser. A failed valve is a common cause of an ice maker that suddenly stops making ice.
install_steps: Unplug the fridge and shut off the household water supply.
Access the valve at the lower rear panel and disconnect the water lines.
Unplug the electrical connectors and remove the mounting bracket.
Install the new valve, reconnect lines and connectors, and restore water and power.

name: Refrigerator Water Filter (Filter 1)
description: Genuine EveryDrop water filter that reduces contaminants and improves taste. Recommended replacement every 6 months.
install_steps: Locate the filter housing (grille or interior upper-right).
Push the release button or turn the old filter a quarter-turn counter-clockwise.
Pull the old filter straight out.
Insert the new filter and turn clockwise until it locks; run 3 gallons of water to flush.

name: Refrigerator Door Gasket Seal
description: OEM magnetic door gasket that maintains the seal between door and cabinet. A torn gasket causes warm spots and frost buildup.
install_steps: Soak the new gasket in warm water to relax it.
Peel back the old gasket to expose the retainer screws and loosen them.
Remove the old gasket and press the new one behind the retainer.
Tighten screws working around the door and check the seal with a dollar-bill test.

name: Dishwasher Drain Pump
description: OEM drain pump that pushes waste water out at the end of a cycle. Replace when the dishwasher leaves standing water in the tub.
install_steps: Cut power and water to the dishwasher.
Remove the lower rack and the bottom spray arm to reach the sump.
Disconnect the drain pump wiring and the drain hose.
Twist out the old pump, install the new one, and reconnect the hose and wiring.

name: Dishwasher Lower Spray Arm
description: OEM lower spray arm that distributes wash water across the bottom rack. Clogged or cracked arms leave dishes dirty.
install_steps: Open the door and pull out the lower rack.
Unscrew or unclip the old spray arm from the center hub.
Seat the new spray arm on the hub and secure it.
Spin it by hand to confirm it rotates freely.

name: Dishwasher Door Latch Assembly
description: OEM door latch with switch. The dishwasher will not start a cycle if the latch fails to signal that the door is closed.
install_steps: Disconnect power to the dishwasher.
Remove the inner door panel screws around the perimeter.
Disconnect the latch wiring and unscrew the old latch.
Install the new latch, reconnect wiring, and reassemble the door panel.

name: Dishwasher Silverware Basket
description: OEM silverware basket with hinged lids. Direct replacement for a cracked or broken basket.
install_steps: Open the dishwasher door and pull out the lower rack.
Lift the old basket out of its holder.
Drop the new basket into place.

name: Dishwasher Heating Element
description: OEM heating element that warms wash water and assists drying. Replace when dishes come out cold and wet.
install_steps: Cut power to the dishwasher and pull it out from the cabinet.
From underneath, disconnect the heating element terminals.
Remove the mounting nuts inside the tub and lift out the old element.
Install the new element, secure the nuts, and reconnect the terminals.
